transcript: Ever wonder how the same ingredients can result in drastically different cookies? Did you guide into what causes different variations in cookies and what to look for in a recipe? For a more standard chewy, soft cookie that spreads, look for a cookie recipe that has a high ratio of fat and sugar to flour. The sugar and fat will cause the cookies to spread more, as there isn't a strong structure to hold the shape. For a thin, delicate, airy, crunchy cookie, choose a recipe that has a low protein flour and reverse creaming. Reverse creaming is when you mix flour and fat together before adding liquids or sugar. The fat coats the flour, creating this barrier from liquid giving the delicate texture for a thick cookie. Choose a recipe that has a higher ratio of flour to sugar and fat. Cream the butter and sugar together, and you want to make sure that the recipe has a high protein flour like bread or whole wheat. Whole wheat absorbs more liquid than all purpose, so it's going to create a chewy cookie that will spread less.
